citation.title: Postprandial Glycemic Response to Whole Fruit versus Blended Fruit in Healthy, Young Adults

reported.what: incremental blood glucose after whole fruit vs blended fruit (gala apple 190 g + blackberries 148 g): maximum, iAUC 0-60 min and 60-min value, all 20 participants and by sex, mean ± SEM, baseline subtracted (Table 1); the meal's available carbohydrate, fat and protein grams are not printed, only an enzyme-assay glucose content

location.quote: mean ± SEM: 1269 ± 124 mg/dL × min for whole fruit vs. 850 ± 109 mg/dL × min for blended fruit

reported.what: baseline blood glucose before each fruit treatment, drawn 3-3.5 h after an undescribed lunch (not a fasting sample)

location.quote: mean ± standard error of the mean (SEM): 102.4 ± 1.8 mg/dL for whole fruit vs. 105.7 ± 1.8 mg/dL for blended fruit

detail: The paper prints only the glucose content of the fruit after invertase (10.03 g per treatment, fructose not counted) and the fibre grams, never the total available carbohydrate, fat or protein of the meal, so the protocol cannot be written; the only values needing no meal (baseline glucose) were drawn 3-3.5 h after an undescribed lunch and are not fasting samples.
